interim_updates.note_text: Teejay Lanka PLC (Group) reported Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026) revenue of Rs.15,636.8mn, down a marginal 0.8% YoY from Rs.15,768.8mn, but swung to a net loss of Rs.479.9mn versus a Rs.207.3mn profit in the prior-year quarter -- a -331.6% swing. The proximate cause is a collapse in gross margin: gross profit fell 74.9% to Rs.313.7mn (from Rs.1,252.0mn), with gross margin compressing from 7.9% to 2.0% of revenue, which management's own commentary attributes to lower sales volumes and pricing pressure from key customers, subdued demand, and disruption from the Strait of Hormuz crisis affecting global supply chains. Distribution expenses fell 16.0% to Rs.136.2mn and administrative expenses fell 2.6% to Rs.932.4mn (cost-transformation and organisational-restructuring initiatives per the commentary), but these savings of only ~Rs.50.8mn combined were dwarfed by the Rs.938.3mn gross-profit decline. A further drag came from net impairment on financial assets, which swung from a Rs.250.6mn reversal (2025) to a Rs.52.3mn provision (2026) -- a Rs.302.9mn negative swing that alone accounts for 27% of the total Rs.1,125.3mn decline in operating result (from a Rs.450.8mn operating profit to a Rs.674.5mn operating loss). Below the operating line, net finance income improved to Rs.18.1mn (from a net finance cost of Rs.86.1mn), a modest Rs.104.1mn favourable swing that partially offset the operating deterioration, on lower finance costs (-34.4% to Rs.120.3mn) and higher finance income (+42.3% to Rs.138.3mn). A Rs.176.6mn tax credit (vs a Rs.157.4mn tax expense prior year) further cushioned the bottom line, but PAT still ended at a Rs.479.9mn loss. No segmental note is presented in this filing so revenue/PBT cannot be broken down by product or geography. On the balance sheet, net asset value per share rose to Rs.47.07 (from Rs.42.95 a year earlier and Rs.44.90 at FYE March 2026), and the cash balance improved to Rs.5,599.9mn (from Rs.5,297.8mn YoY), driven by working-capital-favourable operating cash flow of Rs.2,404.9mn (vs Rs.1,049.0mn prior year) despite the reported net loss -- cash generation was helped by a large positive swing in trade and other payables/receivables movements within working capital, not underlying profitability. Company (standalone) figures show the same pattern: revenue +3.2% to Rs.8,344.7mn but gross profit -83.1% to Rs.130.0mn (margin 1.6% vs 9.5%), and a net loss of Rs.268.2mn versus a Rs.127.8mn profit prior year.

interim_updates.takeaway: The Rs.0.8% revenue decline understates how much underlying trading deteriorated -- gross margin compressed from 7.9% to 2.0% of revenue (gross profit -74.9%), pushing the Group from a Rs.450.8mn operating profit to a Rs.674.5mn operating loss. The reported net loss of Rs.479.9mn would have been considerably worse were it not for a Rs.176.6mn tax credit and a favourable ~Rs.104mn swing in net finance income/(costs) -- neither of which reflects an improvement in the core manufacturing/export business, which remains under real margin and volume pressure (lower sales volumes, customer pricing pressure, and Strait of Hormuz-related supply chain disruption per management's own commentary).
operational_highlights: Group revenue Rs.15,636.8mn, -0.8% YoY (Rs.15,768.8mn) -- broadly flat, but gross profit collapsed 74.9% to Rs.313.7mn as gross margin fell from 7.9% to 2.0% of revenue.
Group swung to a net loss of Rs.479.9mn from a Rs.207.3mn profit in Q1 FY2025/26 (-331.6% YoY); basic loss per share of Rs.(0.67) vs earnings of Rs.0.29 prior year.

Distribution expenses down 16.0% to Rs.136.2mn and administrative expenses down 2.6% to Rs.932.4mn on cost-transformation initiatives, but combined savings of ~Rs.50.8mn were far outweighed by the Rs.938.3mn gross-profit decline.
Net impairment on financial assets swung from a Rs.250.6mn reversal (2025) to a Rs.52.3mn provision (2026), a Rs.302.9mn negative swing that was 27% of the total operating-result decline.
Net finance income/(costs) improved to +Rs.18.1mn from -Rs.86.1mn (finance costs down 34.4% to Rs.120.3mn, finance income up 42.3% to Rs.138.3mn), partially cushioning the bottom line.
Net asset value per share rose to Rs.47.07 (from Rs.42.95 YoY); operating cash flow strengthened to Rs.2,404.9mn (from Rs.1,049.0mn), aided by working-capital movements despite the net loss.
key_drivers: Gross margin compression (7.9% to 2.0% of revenue) on lower sales volumes, customer pricing pressure, subdued demand across key markets, and Strait of Hormuz-related supply-chain disruption -- per management's own commentary, this is the dominant driver of the swing to a net loss.

Net impairment (provision)/reversal on financial assets swung Rs.302.9mn unfavourably (from a Rs.250.6mn reversal to a Rs.52.3mn provision), the second-largest driver of the operating-result decline after gross margin.

A Rs.176.6mn income tax credit (vs a Rs.157.4mn tax expense prior year) and an ~Rs.104.1mn favourable swing in net finance income/(costs) both cushioned the bottom line below the operating loss -- neither reflects improved core trading.
No segmental disclosure is presented in this interim filing, so the revenue/margin deterioration cannot be attributed to specific product lines, customers, or geographies from the source document.
